# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual. The procedure has two stages:
1. First, the key marked with ᘔ must be pressed. Any other touch on the bomb while it is waiting will trigger the fuse.
2. After that key is pressed, the light below indicates which wire to cut:
   - Blue light -> cut green wire
   - Green light -> cut red wire
   - Yellow light -> cut yellow wire

I cannot speak or touch the bomb. I can only gesture to Deaf. However, I currently have no view of the bomb and do not know how the keys are arranged or labelled. Furthermore, no visual protocol has been established with Deaf yet ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). 

Deaf can see the bomb and speak to both Blind and me. I need Deaf to inspect the bomb, describe what they see (the symbols on the keys, wire colors, and layout), and ideally propose a signaling convention. Therefore, I will wait for Blind and Deaf to take their turns in this round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a display, an indicator light, 3 wires (positions 1-3), and a 4-slot keypad (slots 1-4, 1 digit). I can act by cutting wire 1-3 or pressing keypad slot 1-4.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows digit 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. Keypad requires 1 digit, currently entered nothing. Keypad button symbols: Button 1 looks like a reversed or mirrored number 2. Button 2 looks like a spiral or cyclone swirl. Button 3 looks like a reversed capital letter B. Button 4 looks like an upside-down capital letter T.

I have read the defusal manual and Deaf's report of the bomb.

The manual states:
"Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below names the cut."

Deaf reported that Keypad Button 1 looks like a reversed or mirrored number 2, which corresponds directly to the symbol ᘔ (Canadian Syllabics Carrier Z).

I will signal ☝ (1) to Deaf so Deaf knows Button 1 is the key to press first.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signaled the number 1 (☝), but it is not yet clear whether that means Keypad Button 1 or Wire 1. Do NOT touch anything yet. Mute: I am relaying your instructions to Blind, and Blind can speak directly to you since you can hear. To avoid ambiguity, please use a 2-gesture format: use ✌ (scissors) for cutting a wire, and 👆 (point) for pressing a keypad button, followed by the number (☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, etc.). For example: 👆 ☝ for Keypad 1, or ✌ ☝ for Wire 1. What should Blind do?

I need to instruct Blind, via Deaf, to press Keypad button 1 (the key wearing ᘔ, described as a reversed or mirrored number 2).

Following Deaf's proposed convention:
- `👆` means press a keypad button.
- `☝` means slot/position 1.

So I will gesture `👆` followed by `☝` to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute confirmed the action using the protocol: press Keypad Button 1. Please press Keypad Button 1 now.

I must wait for Blind to press Keypad Button 1, after which Deaf can observe the updated status of the indicator light.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: the keypad opens
Deaf says: The keypad opened successfully! Current status: Display is still 0, Light is yellow. Wires remain: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. Mute, please signal the next step: use ✌ followed by wire number (☝, ✌, 🤟) if a wire should be cut, or signal what Blind needs to do.

The keypad has been pressed and opened.
The defusal manual instructs:
"Then the light below names the cut.
| light | cut wire color |
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |"

Deaf confirms the light is yellow. The wire to cut is therefore yellow.
Deaf identified:
- Wire 1: red
- Wire 2: yellow
- Wire 3: green

Wire 2 is yellow. Following Deaf's protocol (✌ for cut wire, followed by the wire index, where ✌ is 2), I will signal `["✌", "✌"]`.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signals [✌ ✌], which means cut Wire 2 (the middle wire, which is yellow). Please cut Wire 2 now.

I will wait for Blind to cut Wire 2.

```
wait()
```
